why: A has an actual design system doing work — one navy accent carried through solid CTA blocks, a consistent white card with an icon tile and an underlined arrow link, real full-colour client marks (Danone, Shin-Line, Hamle), a drawn route-network diagram on a dark panel, and a quote form with labelled fields and honest 'Optional' hints, so the page has a spine and a conversion path. B is a very long document rather than a designed page: nearly the same type size from top to bottom, section after section of the same stacked bordered box or numbered text row, and its only visual device is a small navy 01-08 chip that sits half-over a band edge. The tell that settles it is B's social proof — the client logos are typed uppercase words in empty outlined boxes, ending in one orphan centred box, where A shows the actual logos.
loser_fatal_flaw: B fakes its social proof — the client wall is letterspaced text in empty boxes, not logos — and the rest of the page never rises above a formatted text document, so nothing at all is designed except the numbering.
winner_worst_flaw: A's hero headline is clipped and overlapped by the sticky header and language bar, so the first line of the page is unreadable on arrival; underneath that, the six route cards are mostly empty space with 'Discuss this route' repeated five times.
ai_evidence: Every section wears an identical 01-08 numbered chip in the same navy square, applied uniformly regardless of what the section does
Client logos rendered as uppercase letterspaced text inside plain outlined boxes — the classic placeholder that never got replaced
The same module recycled throughout: a four-item stack of bordered text boxes, then a five-row numbered list, then another four-item stack
Two services sections carry almost the same heading ('...по СНГ и Европе') with near-identical five-row lists beneath them
No hierarchy beyond bold-vs-regular: headings, subheads and body sit at nearly one scale for the whole page
Page length roughly double A's with no visual rest, images or change of rhythm to justify it
